name: subset.steady2D
title: One species of a two-dimensional steady state

origin.description: Returns one species as a matrix with dimens[1] rows and dimens[2] columns.

arguments.name: which
arguments.text: 1-based species index. Selecting more than one variable is an error.

origin.details: The matrix is filled column-major from that species block.
origin.example:
g <- function(t, y, p) {
  Y <- matrix(y, nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
  dY <- Y * 0
  for (i in 1:3) for (j in 1:3) {
    left <- if (i == 1) 0 else Y[i - 1, j]
    right <- if (i == 3) 1 else Y[i + 1, j]
    down <- if (j == 1) 0 else Y[i, j - 1]
    up <- if (j == 3) 0 else Y[i, j + 1]
    dY[i, j] <- left + right + down + up - 4 * Y[i, j]
  }
  list(as.vector(dY))
}
out <- steady.2D(y = rep(0.2, 9), func = g, dimens = c(3, 3))
subset(out)

translation.description: Returns one species as a matrix with dimens[1] rows and dimens[2] columns.

arguments.name: which
arguments.text: 1-based species index. Selecting more than one variable is an error.

translation.details: The matrix is filled column-major from that species block.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from rootSolve import steady_2d, subset_steady2d

def g(t, y, p):
    grid = np.asarray(list(y), dtype=float).reshape((3, 3), order="F")
    change = np.zeros_like(grid)
    for row in range(3):
        for col in range(3):
            left = 0.0 if row == 0 else grid[row - 1, col]
            right = 1.0 if row == 2 else grid[row + 1, col]
            down = 0.0 if col == 0 else grid[row, col - 1]
            up = 0.0 if col == 2 else grid[row, col + 1]
            change[row, col] = left + right + down + up - 4 * grid[row, col]
    return [change.reshape(-1, order="F")]

out = steady_2d([0.2] * 9, func=g, dimens=(3, 3))
print(subset_steady2d(out))
